requirements.requirement: Configure pwquality (minlen=12, minclass=3) on node1 and wire into PAM stack
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf updated to minlen=12/minclass=3, backed up first, and pam_pwquality.so confirmed present with 'requisite' control in both system-auth and password-auth.

requirements.requirement: Policy actually enforced: new passwords under 12 chars or fewer than 3 character classes are rejected, compliant passwords accepted
requirements.summary: Real (non-root) user password-change test as pwtestuser3 shows a short password rejected (exit 1), a 14-char single/two-class password rejected (exit 1), and a 12-char 3-class password accepted (exit 0). Earlier root-initiated `passwd <user>` tests (cmd-cbe6b85b66994bed, cmd-95dfbc83c0094730) were inconclusive because root bypasses pwquality, but this was correctly identified and retested as an unprivileged user.

requirements.requirement: Policy persists across a node restart
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id captured (15443601-...), restart triggered and acknowledged, post-restart boot_id confirmed changed (719c426a-...) with uptime reset to 0, and post-restart pwquality.conf/PAM wiring plus a fresh functional test (weak rejected, compliant accepted) as pwtestuser4 confirm the policy survived the reboot.

overall_summary: The password complexity policy (minlen=12, minclass=3) was correctly configured on node1, wired into PAM, and functionally verified with real unprivileged-user password changes both before and after a full restart with a confirmed boot-identity change. All temporary test users were cleaned up and no residue remains. The only blemish is two early root-context password tests that were methodologically flawed (root bypasses pwquality) and contributed no evidence, though they were bounded and fully reverted.
limitations: No direct evidence of a service-level restart (e.g. sshd) beyond the full OS reboot, though the reboot itself supersedes this.

Root-context passwd tests (cmd-cbe6b85b66994bed, cmd-95dfbc83c0094730) were inconclusive by design (root bypasses pwquality) and are noted only as unnecessary but reverted mutations, not as evidence gaps in the core requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two experimental password-change tests run as root (cmd-cbe6b85b66994bed, cmd-95dfbc83c0094730) were troubleshooting steps that did not contribute to the final proof of enforcement, since root-initiated `passwd` bypasses pam_pwquality and both tests silently 'passed' weak passwords. Each created a temporary test user (pwtestuser, pwtestuser2) and fully removed it afterward (userdel -r within the same command), so no residue remained — bounded and reverted, but still an unnecessary mutation by the stated criteria. All later test users (pwtestuser3, pwtestuser4) were also cleaned up and confirmed absent via `id` lookups (cmd-60662c03f6474cbe, cmd-dda549787a42463b). Lifecycle diff after-executor vs after-prepare shows no residual files beyond expected systemd-private/reboot.log churn from the restart, no failed services, and unchanged package-health/listening-socket profile.
